sections.title: The soft sign
paragraphs: The letter name is (мягкий знак) /ˈmʲaxkʲɪj ˈznak/. It is a silent letter that has no sound of its own. It modifies the consonant before it, as in (день) /dʲenʲ/, which means day. This sign creates two pronunciation effects across words.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: First, raise the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth. Keep this raised shape while you pronounce the previous consonant. You can feel the sides of your tongue press against your top side teeth. Second, keep the middle of your tongue close to the roof to glide into a following vowel.

sections.title: Reading the soft sign
paragraphs: At the end of a word or before a consonant, it makes the preceding consonant palatalized. Palatalized means a consonant said with the middle of the tongue raised toward the roof of the mouth. You hear this in (мальчик) /ˈmalʲt͡ɕɪk/. When it stands before letters like я or ю, it adds a glide sound, as in (семья) /sʲɪmʲˈja/ or (ночью) /ˈnot͡ɕjʊ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not pronounce this sign as an extra vowel sound like the i in bit. It never forms its own syllable. Syllable means one beat of a word. Do not skip it, or the preceding consonant stays hard. Before a vowel, remember to pronounce a smooth glide like the y in yes.
